content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published recommendations in 2016 on antenatal care aimed at ensuring a positive pregnancy experience for women. 2. A WHO fact sheet updated on August 30, 2018, provides guidelines on maintaining a healthy diet, accessible online as of May 21, 2020. 3. The WHO and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations released the second edition of Vitamin and Mineral Requirements in Human Nutrition, which outlines essential nutrient needs. 4. WHO guidelines on vitamin D supplementation for pregnant women are available in a PDF format, accessed on May 21, 2020. 5. Holick MF and Chen TC highlighted the global health consequences of vitamin D deficiency in their 2008 study published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 6. Schoenmakers et al. discussed the prevention and implications of vitamin D deficiency in pregnant and lactating women and children in a 2016 symposium published in the Journal of Steroid Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. 7. Palacios, Kostiuk, and Peña-Rosas reviewed the effects of vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy in a 2019 Cochrane Database systematic review. 8. Bhowmik et al. examined the impact of maternal BMI and nutritional status in early pregnancy on neonatal outcomes in Bangladesh, as published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2019. 9. De-Regil et al. conducted a systematic review on vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy, published in the Cochrane Database in 2016. 10. Vogel et al. described the development and application of living guidelines for WHO recommendations on maternal and perinatal health in a 2019 BMJ Global Health article. 11. The WHO handbook for guideline development, second edition, provides a framework for creating evidence-based health recommendations. 12. The GRADE website offers resources for evaluating the quality of evidence in health research, accessed on May 21, 2020. 13. WHO's declarations of interest, available on their website, outline ethical considerations in guideline development. 14. Downe et al. conducted a scoping review in 2016 to identify processes and outcomes of antenatal care important to healthy pregnant women, published in BJOG. 15. Downe et al. also synthesized qualitative evidence on the provision and uptake of routine antenatal services in a 2019 Cochrane Database review. 16. The GRADE-CERQual website provides tools for assessing the confidence in evidence from qualitative research. 17. The DECIDE project (2011–2015) developed strategies for evidence-based decision-making in healthcare. 18. Cochrane EPOC resources support systematic review authors in evaluating health interventions. 19. Roth et al. conducted the AViDD trial in Bangladesh, assessing high-dose prenatal vitamin D3 supplementation during the third trimester, published in Nutrition Journal in 2013. 20. Roth et al. explored the effects of vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on infant growth in a 2018 New England Journal of Medicine study. 21. Diogenes et al. investigated the effects of calcium and vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy in Brazilian adolescent mothers in a 2013 randomized trial published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 22. Li and Gou studied the prevention of pregnancy-induced hypertension through calcium supplementation in a 2000 study published in the Journal of Xi'an Medical University. 23. Kaur et al. examined the effects of pharmacological doses of vitamin D during pregnancy on placental protein status and birth weight in a 1991 study published in Nutrition Research. 24. Marya et al. evaluated the impact of calcium and vitamin D supplementation on pregnancy toxemia in a 1987 study published in Gynecology and Obstetrics Investigation. 25. Marya et al. also studied the effects of vitamin D supplementation on fetal growth in a 1988 Indian Journal of Medical Research article. 26. Sablok et al. correlated vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy with feto-maternal outcomes in a 2015 Clinical Endocrinology study. 27. Singh et al. reviewed the role of vitamin D in reducing the risk of preterm labor in a 2015 International Journal of Reproductive Contraception Obstetrics and Gynecology article. 28. Asemi et al. assessed the effects of calcium-vitamin D supplementation on metabolic profiles in pregnant women at risk for pre-eclampsia in a 2012 randomized trial published in the Pakistan Journal of Biological Sciences. 29. Asemi et al. also studied the impact of vitamin D supplementation on biomarkers of inflammation, insulin resistance, and oxidative stress in pregnant women in a 2013 Journal of Nutrition article. 30. Mirghafourvand et al. evaluated the effects of vitamin D and calcium plus vitamin D on sleep quality in pregnant women with leg cramps in a 2015 clinical trial published in the Journal of Isfahan Medical School. 31. Naghshineh and Sheikhalian investigated the role of vitamin D supplementation in reducing the risk of preeclampsia in nulliparous women in a 2016 study published in Advances in Biomedical Research. 32. Sabet et al. studied the effects of vitamin D supplementation on maternal and neonatal vitamin D and parathyroid hormone status in pregnant Iranian women in a 2012 Acta Endocrinologica article. 33. Samimi et al. examined the effects of vitamin D plus calcium supplementation on metabolic profiles, inflammation, oxidative stress, and pregnancy outcomes in women at risk for pre-eclampsia in a 2016 Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics article. 34. Samimi et al. also explored the impact of vitamin D supplementation on recurrent spontaneous abortion in a 2017 Global Journal of Health Science article. 35. Sasan et al. evaluated the effects of vitamin D supplementation on preventing recurrent preeclampsia in a 2017 Obstetrics and Gynecology International study. 36. Shahgheibi et al. assessed the impact of vitamin D supplementation on gestational diabetes in high-risk women in a 2016 randomized trial published in the Journal of Research in Medical Sciences. 37. Taherian et al. compared the prevention of preeclampsia using low-dose aspirin or calcium supplementation in a 2002 study published in the Archives of Iranian Medicine. 38. Tehrani et al. studied the effects of vitamin D supplementation on the incidence of gestational diabetes in a 2017 Advances in Biomedical Research article. 39. Vaziri et al. investigated the impact of vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy on infant anthropometric measurements and bone mass in a 2016 Early Human Development study. 40. Khan conducted a randomized controlled trial on oral vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy to improve maternal periodontal health and birth weight, published in the Journal of International Oral Health in 2016. 41. Rodda et al. demonstrated that maternal vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy prevents neonatal vitamin D deficiency in a 2015 Clinical Endocrinology study. 42. Delvin et al. examined the effects of vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy on neonatal calcium homeostasis in a 1986 Journal of Pediatrics article. 43. Mallet et al. compared two methods of vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy in a 1986 Obstetrics and Gynecology study. 44. Grant et al. studied the relationship between vitamin D during pregnancy and infancy and infant serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations in a 2014 Pediatrics article. 45. Mazurkevich et al. analyzed the state of the placental complex during physiological pregnancy with mineral insufficiency correction in a 2013 Journal of Perinatal Medicine abstract. 46. Brooke et al. evaluated the effects of vitamin D supplementation on calcium status and fetal growth in pregnant Asian women in a 1980 British Medical Journal article. 47. Cooper et al. conducted the MAVIDOS trial, assessing maternal gestational vitamin D supplementation and offspring bone health in a 2016 Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology study. 48. Yu et al. investigated vitamin D deficiency and supplementation in pregnant women from four ethnic groups in a 2008 Archives of Disease in Childhood article. 49. WHO issued a recommendation on calcium supplementation during pregnancy to prevent pre-eclampsia and its complications, accessible in PDF format. 50. Palacios et al. reviewed regimens of vitamin D supplementation for pregnant women in a 2019 Cochrane Database systematic review. 51. Kamudoni et al. estimated the economic burden of vitamin D deficiency in pregnant women in the United Kingdom in a 2016 Gynecological Endocrinology article. 52. The British National Formulary provides guidelines on vitamin D supplementation, accessible only from the United Kingdom. 53. WHO, UNICEF, and the United Nations University outlined the composition of a multi-micronutrient supplement for pilot programs among pregnant women in developing countries. 54. The WHO report State of Inequality addresses reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health disparities. 55. Garcia-Casal et al. discussed the implementation of multiple micronutrient supplements in pregnancy as part of quality antenatal care services in a 2018 Maternal and Child Nutrition article.
